summary:
Farmers must decide which crops to rotate while temperatures shift, rainfall becomes unpredictable and soil health declines. We built a rover-and-web solution that turns every 5 m² of a farm into actionable data.

The working prototype is an ESP32-based rover with GPS and temperature and humidity sensors; every reading is tied to its location and mapped on a satellite grid, color-coded by how critical each cell is, with the rover’s position tracked in real time. The full-scale version, designed in CAD, uses an aluminum frame with a suspension for rough terrain, an STM32 controller and a high-current motor driver, plus a charging station where the rover returns to swap its depleted battery.

On the web platform, an AI model combines local readings with NASA Earth observation data and historical records (e.g., vegetation indices, soil moisture, evapotranspiration) to flag plant stress and pests and compare crop-rotation strategies season by season. It also sends alerts with recommended actions and precautions based on the latest measurements and satellite-based predictions, for example warning of a coming frost.

This replaces guesswork with preventive decisions that save water, cut inputs and restore soil health.
details:
Our platform gives farmers real-time analysis of their land at a low cost. On the web tool, the farmer selects a plot and draws its boundary by hand, and the system automatically divides it into a grid. The rover then travels the plot and collects GPS-tagged temperature, humidity and other field data in each cell. An algorithm merges these local readings with NASA satellite data and historical records in our AI model, which generates warnings, risks and the status of every cell. The map shows each cell in a color that reflects how critical it is, and clicking a cell reveals the exact data the rover collected at that point. The system also sends recommended actions and precautions, such as a coming frost, and suggests crop rotations.

Benefits. Large farms are impossible to inspect by hand. Our system lets farmers take preventive action so crops grow in the best conditions and are not lost, saving water, resources and money.

We imagine every farmer, inside and outside the United States, with a work partner that reports the health of each section of their land and forecasts weather and soil conditions, so they can act before problems happen.

Prototype hardware: ESP32 microcontroller, u-blox NEO-6M GPS module, NTC thermistor, DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor, and an L298N motor driver with two DC motors. Full-scale design: STM32 controller, high-current motor driver, aluminum frame with a custom suspension and a battery-swap charging station. Software: Onshape (CAD), EasyEDA (electrical design), Claude Code, GitHub, Arduino IDE and Google Sheets with Apps Script for data logging. Main languages: JavaScript, Python and C/C++.

It is creative in how it collects data (a rover that maps every cell and swaps its own battery), how it represents it (a color-coded grid with click-through details), and how simple it is to use: the farmer only draws their plot and the system does the rest.

We consider low cost, very large plots, rough terrain, continuous operation, ease of use for non-technical farmers, and combining local and satellite data to reduce uncertainty.
